edges.description: Reduced hepatic fibrinogen hexamer synthesis and secretion proportionally lowers functional and antigenic plasma fibrinogen levels.
Proportionally reduced functional and antigenic circulating plasma fibrinogen directly defines the laboratory phenotype of hypofibrinogenemia (<1.5 g/L).
Reduced circulating plasma fibrinogen limits the substrate available for thrombin-mediated conversion to cross-linked fibrin.
Low maternal circulating fibrinogen provides insufficient fibrin/fibrinogen matrix support at the developing uteroplacental interface.
Impaired fibrin clot formation predisposes to a level-dependent bleeding tendency.
A level-dependent bleeding diathesis manifests clinically as variable abnormal bleeding.
In the mild quantitative deficiency state, bleeding is most often provoked by trauma or surgery rather than occurring spontaneously.
Reduced clot stability can manifest as heavy menstrual bleeding in affected women.
Impaired mucosal fibrin hemostasis predisposes symptomatic individuals to epistaxis.
Impaired oral mucosal hemostasis predisposes symptomatic individuals to gingival bleeding.
Impaired gastrointestinal mucosal fibrin hemostasis predisposes symptomatic individuals to gastrointestinal bleeding.
Insufficient fibrinogen compromises placental integrity during pregnancy, producing a spectrum of obstetrical complications.
Defective fibrinogen-mediated uteroplacental attachment directly predisposes to recurrent placental abruption.
